body.text: Maitreyanāthakṛtā Bhavasaṅkrāntiṭīkā
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhavasaṅkrāntiṭīkā</s> (Commentary on the Transition of Existence) composed by <s>Maitreyanātha</s>

body.text: namaḥ sarvajñāya
body.translated_text: Homage to the Omniscient One.

body.text: bhāvābhāvānna janmāsti iti / bījādvīja utpadyamāne ghaṭādapi ghaṭotpattiryujyeta / ātmakriyāniṣedhāt [bījāt] bījotpattirna saṃbhavati / pañcavidhabhūtapariṇāmadharmatā, pratītyasamutpādadharmatā / evaṃ sati śubhāśubhamucchinnabhāraṃ kenacit dṛśyeta / tattu mūṣikādantodgīrṇaviṣameghagarjanaglāna [bīja]vannotpannam / pratītyasamutpādadharmatā / tena na bhāvādutpattidharmatā //
body.translated_text: 'There is no birth from [either] existence or non-existence.' If a seed were to arise from a seed, then the arising of a pot from a pot would also be justified. Because of the negation of self-causation, the arising of a seed from a [prior] seed is not possible. [There is] the nature of transformation of the five elements, [and] the nature of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent arising). This being so, the burden of the wholesome and unwholesome would be seen [to be carried] by someone. But it has arisen like a seed gnawed by a mouse's teeth, weakened by the roar of a cloud of poison. [There is] the nature of dependent arising. Therefore, there is no nature of arising from [inherent] existence.

body.text: tasya bhāvasyacāsataḥ / janmādānaṃ saṃbhavati iti / evaṃ sati bhāvāsyāsata utpattau vandhyāsutaḥ gaganakusumaṃ śaśaśṛṅgañca saṃbhavet / evamasaṃbhavāt utpattirna saṃbhavati / nahyagnimadhye nikṣiptabījasya janma saṃbhavati / ucyate tu bhāvasya tasyāsato janmopādānaṃ bhavati [iti] / yathā prasannajalapūrṇasarasi śaivālaṃ padmañcotpadyate / uttarāraṇyadharāraṇibhyāmagnirutpadyate / utpattau satyāmapi ko doṣaḥ syāt / nityabhāvādutpannātmakamiṣyate / maivam / bhrānti /
body.translated_text: 'And of that entity, being non-existent, birth and reception are possible.' If so — if a non-existent entity could arise — then a barren woman's son, a sky-flower, and a hare's horn would also be possible. Since this is impossible, arising [from non-existence] is not possible. Surely, for a seed placed in fire, birth is not possible. Yet it is said that for that non-existent entity, birth and reception occur. Just as in a lake filled with clear water, moss and lotuses arise; from the upper and lower fire-sticks, fire arises. Even granting arising, what fault would there be? [Objection:] From an eternal entity, it is accepted as having an arisen nature. Not so — this is an error (<s>bhrānti</s>).

children.translated_text: If what is perceived by the senses
were to exist as reality, then children would be knowers of reality — [but] that is not the cause of knowing reality.
[As] stated in the <s>Laṅkāvatārasūtra</s>:
The existence of all entities, as imagined by the childish —
if they were as perceived, all would be seers of reality.

body.text: anyatra uktam / na cakṣuḥ prekṣate rūpaṃ lokastu parimohataḥ / pravartate hyakṣamārge svabhāvastasya tādṛśaḥ //
body.translated_text: Stated elsewhere: 'The eye does not see form, but the world, from delusion, engages in the path of the senses — such is its nature.'

body.text: yathā māyāmarīcisvapnapratiśrutkendradhanurudakacandrabimbanirmitamāyānagaravikalpaḥ /
body.translated_text: Just as the conceptualization of illusion (<s>māyā</s>), mirage (<s>marīci</s>), dream (<s>svapna</s>), echo (<s>pratiśrutkā</s>), rainbow (<s>indradhanus</s>), the moon's reflection in water (<s>udakacandrabimba</s>), and a magically created city (<s>nirmitamāyānagara</s>).

body.text: śūrapādairapyuktam /
body.translated_text: As also stated by <s>Śūrapāda</s>:

children.text: sadasacca mṛtaṃ jātaṃ tannirūddha yadasti na /
children.translated_text: 'Existent and non-existent, dead and born, that which has ceased yet does not exist —
is productive of existence' — this is the characteristic [view] of those who see [inherent] existence.

body.text:
bhāvadṛṣṭyā khalu bhrāntaṃ yathā khapuṣpacintanam /
dharmatā hi nabhastulyā / iti /
body.translated_text: Indeed, from the perspective of [inherent] existence, [all] is erroneous, like the thought of a sky-flower. For the nature of reality (<s>dharmatā</s>) is like space.

body.text: ākāśasamabhāvasya śūnyatvena utpattibhaṅgadoṣamalālepāt dharmatāmātraṃ rūpavedanādayaḥ / te gaganasamāḥ / jananāntare pratītyasamāgamenotpadyante / tacca sāṃvṛt loke / paramārthasya na virodhi / acintyā māyādharmalakṣaṇatā / śālistambasūtre /
body.translated_text: The nature of existence being equal to space — through emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), [there being] no stain of the fault of arising and destruction — form, feeling, and the rest are mere reality-nature (<s>dharmatā</s>). They are equal to space. In another birth, they arise through the conjunction of conditions. And that is conventional (<s>sāṃvṛta</s>) in the world; it does not contradict the ultimate (<s>paramārtha</s>). The nature of the quality of reality as illusion (<s>māyā</s>) is inconceivable. In the <s>Śālistambasūtra</s>:

body.text: [bāhyaḥ] pratītyasamutpādaḥ katamaiḥ pañcabhiḥ kāraṇairdraṣṭavyaḥ / [na] svayaṃ śāśvatato nocchedato na saṃkrāntito na svayaṃbhūhetutaḥ na phalavipākābhinirvṛttitastadvisadṛśānuprabandhata [śceti] / kathaṃ [na] svayaṃ śāśvatataḥ / yasmādvījāṅkurau visadṛśau / na caivaṃ yadvījaṃ sa evāṅkura [iti] / evaṃ hi bījaṃ niruddhyate / aṅkura utpadyate / kathaṃ nocchedataḥ / na pūrvaniruddhāddhījādaṅkuro niṣpadyate / niruddhamatrādvījāttu tatsamaye aṅkura utpadyate / tulādaṇḍanāmonnāmavat / kathaṃ na saṅkrāntitaḥ / bījavisadṛśo hyaṅkuraḥ / kathaṃ na svayaṃbhūhetutaḥ / ādyaphalasyāsvayaṃbhāvāt / kathaṃ na phalavipākābhinirvṛttitaḥ / phalasvarūpaṃ siddhyati / na hi phalena phalotpattirasti / kathaṃ visadṛśānuprabandhataḥ / evaṃ pratītya samutpannaistairutpāditaṃ phalam //
body.translated_text: By which five causes should external <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent arising) be viewed? [It is] not from eternality by itself, not from annihilation, not from transmigration, not from a self-caused (<s>svayaṃbhū</s>) cause, not from the production of the ripening of fruit, [but] from the continuation of what is dissimilar. How not from eternality by itself? Because the seed and sprout are dissimilar — it is not the case that the seed itself is the sprout. Thus, the seed ceases; the sprout arises. How not from annihilation? The sprout is not produced from a seed that has previously ceased; rather, the sprout arises at the very moment when the seed has just ceased — like the rising and falling of the beam of a balance. How not from transmigration? Because the sprout is dissimilar from the seed. How not from a self-caused cause? Because the first fruit does not come into being by itself. How not from the production of the ripening of fruit? The own-nature of the fruit is established [independently]; for there is no arising of a fruit from a [prior] fruit. How from the continuation of the dissimilar? Thus, the fruit is produced by those that have arisen dependently.

body.text: skandhotpādarītirapiu / avidyayā saṃskāro vijñānaṃ nāmarūpaṃ ṣaḍāyatanaṃ pañcaskandhāśca siddhyanti /
body.translated_text: The method of the arising of the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>) also [follows this]: through <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations), <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form), <s>ṣaḍāyatana</s> (six sense-bases), and the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) are established.

children.translated_text: That the arising of those whose nature is such [occurs] through empty [conditions] alone —
arisen dependently from conditions — is thus established through [this] proof.

children.text: evaṃ sā śūnyatā svayaṃbhūtvā rūpaṃ samīkṣyate /
children.translated_text: Thus, that <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), being self-existent, is seen as form;
all existence is <s>śūnyatā</s>, and <s>śūnyatā</s> thus operates.

body.text: evaṃ bāhya ādhyātmikaḥ sarvo dharmaḥ śūnyaḥ / svabhāvato bhāvo yena hetusaṃbhūtaḥ ataḥ sarvadharma ākāśasamaḥ / evaṃ bhāvo 'bhāvaḥ saṃbhavati //
body.translated_text: Thus, all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena), both external and internal, are empty. An entity that has arisen from causes is [empty] by its own nature — therefore all <s>dharmas</s> are equal to space. Thus, existence [itself] becomes non-existence.

body.text: na kāraṇaṃ nāpi kāryam ityādinā eṣa lokaḥ paro 'pi ca iti paryantam / kāraṇena īśvareṇa kṛta iṣyate / karmasaṃbhūtaḥ cittamātraṃ vā iṣyate / evaṃ neṣyate cet kaḥ śubhāśubhaṃ vahati / tīrthikocchedaprasaṅgaḥ / tasyottara [mucyate] / vastutaḥ satyaṃ na bhavati [lokaḥ] / karmasaṃbhūto 'pi svapnasadṛśaḥ /
body.translated_text: [The passage] beginning with 'neither cause nor effect' up to 'this world and the next' [is discussed]. [Some hold that the world] is accepted as created by a cause, namely <s>Īśvara</s> (God). [Others hold that it] arises from <s>karma</s> (action). Or [still others hold that it is] <s>cittamātra</s> (mind-only). If it is not accepted thus, then who carries the wholesome and unwholesome [karma]? [This would lead to] the absurd consequence of the annihilationism of the non-Buddhist schools (<s>tīrthika</s>). The reply to that [objection is given]: In reality, [the world] does not truly exist. Though arisen from <s>karma</s>, it is like a dream.

children.translated_text: An entity, precisely because of its non-existence in this way, is unborn and non-existent for a long time;
but at the time of arising through conditions (<s>pratītya</s>), there is the experience of the fruit of <s>karma</s> (action).
In the <s>Ārya-Samādhirāja-sūtra</s>:

children.text: na ca asmi loki mṛti kaści [naro] paraloka saṃkramati gacchati vā /
children.translated_text: No person in this world dies and transmigrates or goes to another world;

children.text: na ca karma naśyati kadāci kṛtaṃ phalu deti [kṛṣṇaśubha] saṃsarato //
children.translated_text: nor does <s>karma</s> (action) once performed ever perish — it bears fruit, [whether] dark or wholesome, in <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence).
In the <s>Laṅkāvatāra-sūtra</s>:
I always teach emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), free from eternalism and annihilationism;

children.text: saṃsāraṃ svapnamāyākhyaṃ na ca karma vinaśyati //
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃsāra</s> is called a dream and an illusion (<s>māyā</s>), yet <s>karma</s> does not perish.
In the <s>Ārya-Ākāśasamatā-samādhi-sūtra</s>:

children.text: pūrvaṃ kṛtaṃ tanna kṛtaṃ na kṛtaṃ tacchubhāśubham /
children.translated_text: What was done before — that is both done and not done; that wholesome or unwholesome [action] —

children.text: sugatasya pūrvākaraṇāt kṛtaṃ tadapi no bhavet //
children.translated_text: because the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One) did not previously make it, that which was done also would not exist.
The <s>bodhicitta</s> (mind of awakening) of a <s>Bodhisattva</s> — though done, it also would not exist;

children.text: kṛto nirūḍhilābho 'pi kṛtaḥ so 'pi ca no bhavet //
children.translated_text: the attainment of firm establishment — though done, it also would not exist.
<s>Karmas</s> (actions) do not perish even after hundreds of millions of <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic ages);
at the time of coming together through conditions, there is the experience of the fruit for embodied beings.

body.text: anutpannarūpameva / iti /
body.translated_text: The nature [of all this] is indeed unborn (<s>anutpanna</s>). Thus [it is said].

body.text: yadīśvareṇa kathamapi na nirmitam / kathaṃ hi loka utpannaḥ /
body.translated_text: If [the world is] not created by <s>Īśvara</s> (God) in any way, then how has the world arisen?

body.text: vandhyāstrītanayasyāpi kastatra janma janayati /
body.translated_text: Even for the son of a barren woman, who in that case brings about his birth?

body.text: lokaḥ prathamato 'jātaḥ ityādi /
body.translated_text: [It is said:] 'The world is primordially unborn,' and so forth.

body.text: ādau svayamanutpannaḥ pratītyasamutpanno bhāvaḥ / tasya ca janma īśvarādinā kenāpi nāvatāritam / cetanasyādāvajātatvena īśvaraḥ svayamasiddhaḥ / pratītyasamutpannasya ca janma neśvareṇāvatāritam / laṅkāvatārasūtre /
body.translated_text: In the beginning, an entity is itself unborn — it is dependently originated (<s>pratītyasamutpanna</s>). And its birth has not been brought about by anyone, whether <s>Īśvara</s> or any other. Since a conscious being is in the beginning unborn, <s>Īśvara</s> is himself unestablished. And the birth of what is dependently originated has not been brought about by <s>Īśvara</s>. In the <s>Laṅkāvatāra-sūtra</s>:

children.translated_text: The childish see origination and destruction out of delusion;

children.text: na saṃbhavaṃ na vibhavaṃ prajñāyukto vipaśyati //
children.translated_text: one endowed with wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) sees neither origination nor destruction.
In the <s>Ārya-Samādhirāja-sūtra</s>:

children.text: astīti nāstīti ubhe 'pi antā śuddhī aśuddhīti ime 'pi antā /
children.translated_text: 'Exists' and 'does not exist' — both are extremes; 'pure' and 'impure' — these too are extremes.

children.text: tasmādubhe anta vivarjayitvā madhye 'pi sthānaṃ na karoti paṇḍitaḥ //
children.translated_text: Therefore, having abandoned both extremes, the wise one does not take a stand even in the middle.
[From the] <s>Madhyānta</s> [?]:

children.text: yena tarkaḥ kalpamātraṃ talliṅgaṃ niṣphalaṃ sthitam /
children.translated_text: Reasoning by which is mere conceptual construction — the inferential mark of that remains fruitless;
thus it is stated by the wise: 'The lowest is destroyed by conceptualization.'
By examining, one is liberated; and by the [proper] action regarding the world;
the <s>yogin</s> (practitioner) perceives [all as] empty (<s>śūnya</s>), like one who sees in the dark.
Through the application of medicine, one should see [clearly]; and one should cast off that cataract (<s>timira</s>).
[Those] whose eyes are overcome by the cataract of ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) — [grasping] origination and destruction firmly —

body.text: gṛhṇanto vāsanāvaśāt muktyanarhāḥ samīritāḥ //
body.translated_text: grasping due to the force of latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), they are declared to be unworthy of liberation.

body.text: anarthabhrāntaloko hi ityādyuktam /
body.translated_text: [It is said:] 'The world, deluded about what is harmful,' and so forth.

body.text: kārakavedayitrādi na kiñcidasti / mokṣārthākārake paramārthabhrāntaḥ / athavā anarthaṃ bhraman bhavasindhurmāyānagarasadṛśaḥ /
body.translated_text: There is no agent, experiencer, or anything [of the sort]. One who is deluded in the ultimate sense about the agent [who is supposed to work] for the sake of liberation — or alternatively: the ocean of existence (<s>bhavasindhu</s>), wandering in what is harmful, is like an illusory city (<s>māyānagara</s>).

body.text:
uktamāryadevapādaiḥ /
bhāvo 'bhāvo na dvitayaṃ sadasanmiśrito na saḥ /
nāpi tattadabhāvādi vicāre 'pi ciraṃ kṛte /
tatpadamatidurbhāṣam /
body.translated_text: The venerable <s>Āryadeva</s> has stated: 'Neither existence nor non-existence, nor both, nor a mixture of real and unreal — nor is it [defined by] the absence of each of those. Even after prolonged investigation, that state is extremely difficult to express.'

body.text: sadasadutpannavinaṣṭayat kiñcidbhāvavarjanadharmanairātmyadeśanā parivartaḥ prathamaḥ //
body.translated_text: The teaching of the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmanairātmya</s>), which avoids any entity whatsoever — whether existent or non-existent, arisen or destroyed — [this is] the first chapter.

body.text: adhunā skandhanairātmyaṃ pratipādayan saṃvṛtisatyamāśrityāha lokotpattirītim /
body.translated_text: Now, in order to establish the selflessness of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), relying on conventional truth (<s>saṃvṛtisatya</s>), [the text] states the manner of the world's origination:

body.text: vikalpāllokasaṃbhavaḥ iti /
body.translated_text: 'From conceptualization (<s>vikalpa</s>), the world arises.'

body.text: śubhāśubhakalpanā vikalpaḥ / tatpratītyasamutpanno lokaḥ / śubhāśubhābhyāṃ ṣaṭsu jagadgatiṣu skandhanupādāya loko nāma, vikalpena janitaḥ / salilaphalādivikalpaśca pratītya gṛhyate / janmopādānena cittaṃ pravartane / citte ātmagrahaḥ pravartate / tato 'nyadapi pravartate /
body.translated_text: The conceptualization of wholesome and unwholesome — that is <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual construction). The world arises in dependence on that. Through the wholesome and the unwholesome, in the six destinations (<s>gati</s>) of the world, having taken up the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), what is called 'the world' is produced by conceptualization. And the conceptualization of water, fruit, and the like is grasped in dependence [on conditions]. By the taking up of birth, the mind (<s>citta</s>) operates. In the mind, grasping at a self (<s>ātmagraha</s>) operates. From that, other [afflictions] too operate.

children.translated_text: And that is stated in the <s>Ratnāvalī</s>:
As long as there is grasping at the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), just so long [there is the thought] 'I';

children.text: ahaṅkāre sati punaḥ karma janma tataḥ punaḥ //
children.translated_text: when there is ego-grasping (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>), there is again <s>karma</s> (action), and from that, birth again.
This triple-pathed [cycle], without beginning, end, or middle — the circle of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) —
resembling a whirling firebrand (<s>alātamaṇḍala</s>), it revolves, each [factor] being the cause of the others.

body.text:
cittātkāyo 'pi jāyate / iti /
ātmani sati parasaṃjñā svaparavibhāgātparigrahadveṣau /
anayoḥ saṃpratibaddhāḥ sarve doṣāḥ prajāyante /
kāye kṛtaparīkṣamātre cittamātramataṃ parīkṣitapūrvavat vidyat /
bāhyaḥ skandhaḥ parīkṣyate / rūpavedanāsaṃjñāśca iti /
body.translated_text: The body too arises from the mind. Thus: when there is a self, there arises the notion of 'other'; from the distinction of self and other arise grasping and aversion; bound to these two, all faults arise. When the body alone has been examined, the doctrine of mind-only (<s>cittamātra</s>) should be known as already examined. The external <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) are [now] examined — namely <s>rūpa</s> (form), <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), and <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception).

body.text: rūpaṃ bhautikaṃ / rūpaṃ varṇādyātmakaṃ sadasadubhayānubhayaṃ hetujanitaṃ prajñaptimātram / asatyatayā tarkākṣamatvāt phenasadṛśaṃ śūnyatā / vedanā sukhaduḥkhātmikā / sā ca pratītyasamutpannā asatkāraṇā budbudopamā / saṃjñā hi na sadvastu / sā hi nāmamātram / marīcikāsadṛśī asatī / saṃskāro 'pi asadvastu, bhojanapānatṛṣṇāsukhajanitaḥ / tacca pṛthivyādibhūtapratyayena / sa ca nirvikalpo bhāvaḥ kadalīsamaḥ / tadvijñānaṃ cittamasvatantrotpannalakṣaṇam / cittaṃ vikalpamātraṃ māyopamaṃ, paramārthato nāsti / [prajñā] pāramitāyāmapyuktam / cittaṃ sadasadanyasvabhāvarahitaṃ śūnyam / citena citte dṛṣṭamātre na kiñciddṛśyate, śūnyam //
body.translated_text: <s>Rūpa</s> (form) is material. Form, whose nature is color and the like, is neither existent, nor non-existent, nor both, nor neither — it is produced by causes and is mere designation (<s>prajñaptimātra</s>). Being unreal, since it cannot withstand logical analysis, it is like foam — [this is] <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness). <s>Vedanā</s> (feeling) has the nature of pleasure and pain. It too is dependently arisen (<s>pratītyasamutpanna</s>), without real cause, like a water bubble. <s>Saṃjñā</s> (perception) is indeed not a real entity. It is mere name; like a mirage, it is unreal. <s>Saṃskāra</s> (formations) too are not real entities, born from the thirst for food, drink, and pleasure. And that [arises] from the condition of the elements such as earth and the like. It is a state without conceptual construction (<s>nirvikalpa</s>), like a plantain tree. That <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) is mind, characterized by arising dependently. Mind is mere conceptual construction (<s>vikalpamātra</s>), like an illusion (<s>māyā</s>) — ultimately it does not exist. In the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> too it is said: mind, devoid of the nature of existent, non-existent, other, or self, is empty. When mind is seen by mind as mere seeing, nothing is seen — it is empty.

body.text: evaṃ sati tathāgataḥ jaḍaḥ syāt / maivam / citavijñānavikalpanivṛttikālamātre dharmakāyo labhyate / buddhapadalābha eva jñānakāyaḥ / sa ca nāsti sa īdṛśo bhāva iti / na ca evaṃ sa jñeya iti / na ca sthātā / nāpi sthitiḥ / śavabhūtānaṃ pramāṇakṛtāṃ bālānāṃ vikalpaḥ / tathāgato hyatītānāgatapratyutpannajñaḥ abhijñācakṣuṣā sarvaṃ paśyati //
body.translated_text: If this is so, the <s>Tathāgata</s> would be inert. Not so! At the very moment of the cessation of conceptual construction of mind and consciousness, the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (truth body) is attained. The attainment of the stage of <s>Buddha</s> is itself the <s>Jñānakāya</s> (knowledge body). And it does not exist as such a [fixed] entity. Nor should it be known in this way. Nor does it remain. Nor is there permanence. The conceptual construction of childish beings who are like corpses, [relying on] valid means of knowledge. For the <s>Tathāgata</s>, knowing the past, future, and present, sees everything with the eye of <s>abhijñā</s> (superknowledge).

body.text: caittaṃ cittavikalpaḥ / parīkṣā tu pūrvavat /

children.translated_text: Form is like a mass of foam; feeling is like a water bubble;
perception is like a mirage; formations are like a plantain tree;
and consciousness is like an illusion — [thus] declared by the Kinsman of the Sun [<s>Āditya</s>].

body.translated_text: The mental factor (<s>caitta</s>) is a conceptual construction of the mind. The examination is as before.

body.text: skandhanairātmyavijñānairātmyabhāvo vikalpaḥ / siddhaḥ / yato nāsti vandhyāduhitṛbhartṛvat //
body.translated_text: The selflessness of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) [and] the state of selflessness of consciousness is [mere] conceptual construction — this is established, since [it] does not exist, like the husband of a barren woman's daughter.

body.text: skandhanairātmyadeśanaparivarto dvitīyaḥ /
body.translated_text: This is the second chapter on the teaching of the selflessness of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates).

body.text: nairātmyadvayaṃ saṃgṛhya adhunā prajñotpādārthamāha /
body.translated_text: Having summarized the twofold selflessness (<s>nairātmya</s>), [the text] now speaks for the purpose of generating <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom):

body.text: cittābhāvānna dharmo 'pi / ityādi /
body.translated_text: Since mind does not exist, <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) too [do not exist]. And so forth.

body.text: dharmaḥ bhāvaḥ kṛtakākṛtakarāśiḥ / tatha pṛthivīdhātvādirapi / dharmāṇāṃ mūlaṃ cittamiti cittaṃ niṣiddham / caittadharmatāyāmuttaraṃ ākṣepoktikathitam /
body.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> (phenomenon) is an entity, the aggregate of the made and unmade. Likewise the earth element and the rest. The root of <s>dharmas</s> is the mind — thus the mind has been negated. Regarding the nature of mental factors (<s>caitta</s>), the reply has been stated in the form of an objection.

children.translated_text: Elsewhere the <s>Buddha</s> has said:

children.text: anakṣarasya tattvasya śrutiḥ kā deśanā ca kā /
children.translated_text: Of the reality that is without syllables, what hearing and what teaching can there be?
The meaning is heard and taught [only through] sameness (<s>samatā</s>), for that indeed is without syllables.
Moreover, the <s>Buddha</s> has said:
Without relying on conventional practice (<s>saṃvṛticaryā</s>), the ultimate truth (<s>paramārtha</s>) is not taught;
without knowing the ultimate, <s>nirvāṇa</s> is not attained.
Furthermore, it is said in the <s>śāstra</s> (treatise):
That which is <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), we declare to be <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness);
for whatever arises dependently, that is not arisen from its own nature.

children.text: pratītyopādāya jātaṃ yat[tat] śūnyaṃ hi pracakṣmahe /
children.translated_text: That which has arisen dependently and by appropriation, that we declare to be empty;
whoever understands <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), that person is a vigilant wise one (<s>paṇḍita</s>).

body.text: [iti] bahūktirnirarthikā / evamadvayamārgeṇa sarvajñānaṃ buddhasādhanam / tasya mārgamimaṃ niścitya jñānārthaṃ ya advayamārgaḥ sa svayamadvayaḥ / athavā utpattivināśābhāvena sadasannityānityabhāvābhāvādidvayapratītyabhāvāt advayajñānam / evañcādvayaṃ, tadubhayasaṃśayānabhidhānaṃ prajñāpāramitājñānam / tat jñātvā yaḥ sākṣātkaroti sa tatvajñānāt buddho bhagavān / sa buddhaḥ karuṇābalena provāca / yāvadavidyāstitvaṃ janmaparigrahaḥ / avidyādito nivṛttamatraṃ cet jñānaṃ tattvajñaḥ [syāt] iti //
body.translated_text: Thus many statements are purposeless [without understanding]. In this way, through the non-dual path (<s>advayamārga</s>), omniscience (<s>sarvajñāna</s>) is the means of attaining <s>Buddhahood</s>. Having determined this path, the non-dual path for the sake of knowledge is itself non-dual. Or alternatively, due to the absence of arising and destruction, and hence the absence of dualities such as existent and non-existent, permanent and impermanent, being and non-being — [there is] non-dual knowledge. Thus the non-dual, being the non-assertion of both [extremes] along with their doubt, is the knowledge of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom). Having known that, one who directly realizes it, through the knowledge of reality (<s>tattvajñāna</s>), is the <s>Buddha Bhagavān</s> (Blessed Lord). That <s>Buddha</s>, by the power of compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), declared: as long as ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>) persists, there is grasping of birth. When there is merely the cessation beginning from ignorance, then knowledge [arises and one] becomes a knower of reality.

body.text: anādhāramidaṃ sarvam / iti /
body.translated_text: All this is without foundation. Thus:

body.text: nirādhārakaruṇāprajñācakṣuṣā nirātmakam / śūnyatākārakavedakavastvādhārābhāvakaruṇāprajñācakṣuṣā nirātmakam / śūnyatākārakavedakavastu ādhāro nāsti / idaṃ sarvaṃ traidhātukamaśeṣamasat śūnyatā / sa hi paramārthaḥ / prajñāpāramitāyāmapyuktam /
body.translated_text: Without foundation — through the eye of compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>) and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), [all is seen as] selfless. The entity that is the perceiver and perceived of the form of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) has no foundation. All this, the entire triple world (<s>traidhātuka</s>) without remainder, is non-existent — [this is] <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness). This indeed is the ultimate truth (<s>paramārtha</s>). In the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> too it is said:

body.text: subhūtimavocat / rūpaṃ na prekṣate / ityādi /
body.translated_text: He said to <s>Subhūti</s>: 'He does not behold form.' And so forth.

body.text: dvādaśapratītyasamutpādaniṣedhadharmatāyām /
body.translated_text: Regarding the nature of the negation of the twelve[-fold] dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>):

body.text: buddhaguṇanītabhāgīyaṃ dharmakāyaṃ śūnyatāvastu pracakṣate / tena hi prajñāpāramitā //
body.translated_text: They declare the <s>dharmakāya</s> (truth-body), which partakes of the qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>, to be the foundation of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>). For that is the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom).

body.text: prajñādeśanāparivartastṛtīyaḥ
body.translated_text: The third chapter: the section on the teaching of <s>Prajñā</s> (Wisdom).

body.text: evaṃ prajñāṃ deśayitvā adhunā saṃvṛtāvupāyo deśyate /
body.translated_text: Having thus taught <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), now the method (<s>upāya</s>) in conventional [truth] (<s>saṃvṛti</s>) is taught.

body.text:
dānaśīlakṣametyādi /
sūrye uditamatre chāyotpattivadupāya uktaḥ / prathamaṃ dānaṃ mūlamidhīyate / uktamanyatra /
body.translated_text: 'Generosity (<s>dāna</s>), morality (<s>śīla</s>), patience (<s>kṣama</s>)' and so forth. Just as when the sun has merely risen a shadow appears, so the method is stated. First, generosity (<s>dāna</s>) is established as the root. As stated elsewhere:

children.translated_text: This entire world desires happiness alone;
for people deprived of enjoyments (<s>bhoga</s>), from where can the hope of happiness be obtained?

body.text: dānotsargeṇa hi bhoga utpadyate / tena dānaṃ mūlamuktam / dānāni catvāri / dharmāmiṣābhayamaitrīti / rājyasvaśiraḥparyantamavaradharmadānam / [tathā hi] dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ maṇiḥ muktā pravālaḥ rathaḥ gajaḥ bhṛtyaḥ dāsaḥ dāsīū priyabhāryā duhitṛsutaḥ pradhānasvaṃ, śiraḥ karṇaḥ nāsā pāṇiḥpādaḥ cakṣuḥ svamāṃsaṃ raktaṃ astimajjā medaḥ tvak hṛdayamātmīyaṃ vastu sarvaṃ dadyāt / nanvevaṃ sati bodhisattvacaryā nātiduṣkarā? kuśalopāyo hi buddhalābhakaraḥ / buddhasukhañca nistulaṃ sukham / duḥkhaśataiścaryāpi duḥkhaṃ na syāt / tadyathā ekaputravadhasamaye pitra vikriyate / cittabhyāsamātre tu nāśakathaṃ kiñcidapi / mayūrasya śarīrabhedādahiviṣamamṛtaṃ [bhavati] / viṣañca tadabhyāsāt rasāyanaṃ bhavati / ānandaviśeṣasukhajanakañca / yadabhyastaṃ tadamṛtaṃ bhavati / tena duḥkhaṃ cittavikalpaḥ //
body.translated_text: For through the relinquishing of gifts, enjoyment (<s>bhoga</s>) arises. Therefore, generosity (<s>dāna</s>) is said to be the root. There are four [types of] giving: <s>dharma</s> (teaching), <s>āmiṣa</s> (material goods), <s>abhaya</s> (fearlessness), and <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness). The lower giving of <s>dharma</s> extends from one's kingdom and possessions up to one's own head. [That is to say]: one should give wealth, grain, gold, silver, gems, pearls, coral, chariots, elephants, servants, male and female slaves, beloved wife, daughter, son, one's chief possessions, one's head, ears, nose, hands, feet, eyes, one's own flesh, blood, bones, marrow, fat, skin, heart — all that belongs to oneself. But if so, would not the <s>bodhisattva</s> practice be extremely difficult? Skillful means (<s>kuśalopāya</s>) is what brings about the attainment of <s>Buddha</s>-hood. And the happiness of a <s>Buddha</s> is incomparable happiness. Even a practice [involving] hundreds of sufferings would not be suffering [in comparison]. Just as a father is tormented at the time of the killing of his only son — but through mere mental training (<s>cittābhyāsa</s>), nothing whatsoever is intolerable. Just as the peacock's body transforms snake-venom into nectar, and poison through habituation becomes an elixir, a generator of special bliss and happiness — what is habituated to becomes nectar. Therefore suffering is [merely] a mental construction (<s>cittavikalpa</s>).

body.text: śīlopāyaḥ / śīlābhidhā ca caryāsti daśākuśalavarjitā / prātimokṣasaṃvararakṣaṇam, sarvaprāṇyupakāramaitracittavattvam, svabhoge alaṃbuddhiḥ, abrahmacaryavarjanam, satyavacanamevaṃ karomīti, apāruṣyavacanam, parārādhanam, dharmaśo vinayacaryābhāṇakasya sagauravabhāṣaṇam, pareṇātmagrahaṇe alobhaḥ, kāmacittānāmanutpādanam, yātrādya dbhuta [darśana]varjanam, ākarṣaṇaśāṭhyavirahaḥ, triṣu buddhadharmasaṅgheṣu adhimukticittatvam, sarveṣāṃ sattvānāṃ buddhakaraṇe mahotsāhaḥ //
body.translated_text: The method of morality (<s>śīla</s>): The practice called morality is [conduct that is] free from the ten unwholesome actions (<s>daśākuśala</s>): the guarding of the <s>prātimokṣa</s> (monastic) vow, having a mind of friendliness (<s>maitrī</s>) toward the welfare of all living beings, contentment with one's own possessions, avoidance of unchastity (<s>abrahmacaryavarjana</s>), truthful speech such as 'I shall do thus,' non-harsh speech, serving others, respectful speaking toward one who recites the <s>dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> practices, non-greed when others seize one's possessions, non-arising of lustful thoughts, avoidance of gazing at wondrous spectacles during travel, freedom from deception and fraud, having a mind of aspiration (<s>adhimukti</s>) toward the three — <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṅgha</s>, and great enthusiasm in leading all beings to <s>Buddha</s>-hood.

body.text:
dānaśīlādinā ciramarjite 'pi puṇye yadi kṣāntirnāsti / tadā sadya eva puṇyaṃ naśyet /
uktañca śāntidevena /
body.translated_text: Even if merit has been accumulated over a long time through generosity (<s>dāna</s>), morality (<s>śīla</s>), and the rest, if there is no patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), that merit would be destroyed immediately. As <s>Śāntideva</s> has said:

children.translated_text: All that well-accumulated good conduct — generosity, worship of the <s>Sugatas</s> —
performed over thousands of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), a single [moment of] anger (<s>pratigha</s>) destroys.

children.text: na ca dveṣasamaṃ pāpaṃ na ca kṣāntisamaṃ tapaḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no sin equal to hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>), and no austerity (<s>tapas</s>) equal to patience (<s>kṣānti</s>);
therefore one should cultivate patience with effort, through various methods.

body.text: iti /
body.translated_text: Thus.

body.text: tisraḥ kṣāntayaḥ / duḥkhādhivāsanākṣāntiḥ parābhavamarṣaṇakṣāntiḥ dharmanidhyānakṣāntiśceti / tatra prathamā kasyādhivacanam / evaṃ- ahaṃ te anuttaradharma samyaksaṃbuddhalābhaṃ karomi bodhisattvacaryaviśuddhiñca karomi / [ityukte kaścidāha]mayoktaṃ śṛṇu / no cet jvalanmahāvanhau praviśya prajvala / duḥkhamutpannaṃ kāyo vahatu / tasyaivamuttaraṃ vadāmi / evaṃ satyapi atyantamutsahe / ahamanuttaradharma [samyak] saṃbuddha[lābha]āya bodhisattvacaryāśodhanāya ca trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātau agnijvālā bhūtvā brahmabhavana[paryantaṃ] svataḥ paripācayāmi / kaḥpunarvādastvaduktavanhiḥ // parābhibhavamarṣaṇakṣāntiḥ, parīkṣayā [apakāriṣu] apradarśitakopaḥ āyudhena māṃse chinne 'pi adhyadhikāṃ kṣāntiṃ janayitvā ahaṃ śata[dhā] hastacchedakamapi śirasi vahāmi taduparyapi maitracittayuktaḥ / iti // dharmanidhyānakṣāntiḥ atigambhīre yāne atiśobhane munidharme prathamato labdhe kṣaṇamapi kiñcidasandigdhacittatvam / dharmanidhyānakṣāntividhistu parābhibhavamarṣaṇakṣāntivat / dharmābhāvaścādharo 'tra viśeṣaḥ // vīryaṃ śāntidevenoktam /
body.translated_text: There are three types of patience (<s>kṣānti</s>): patience in enduring suffering (<s>duḥkhādhivāsanākṣānti</s>), patience in tolerating the abuse of others (<s>parābhavamarṣaṇakṣānti</s>), and patience in contemplating the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmanidhyānakṣānti</s>). Regarding the first — what is it an expression of? Thus: 'I will accomplish for you the attainment of unsurpassed perfect <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>-hood, and I will purify the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct.' [When this is said, someone says:] 'Listen to what I say. If not, enter a blazing great fire and be consumed. Let the body endure the suffering that arises.' To this I reply: 'Even so, I am extremely zealous. For the sake of attaining unsurpassed perfect awakening and for purifying the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct, I will become a mass of flames throughout the three-thousand great-thousand world-system up to the <s>Brahmā</s>-abode and ripen [beings] by my own [power]. How much less, then, the fire you describe!' Patience in tolerating the abuse of others (<s>parābhavamarṣaṇakṣānti</s>): by examination, showing no anger toward those who harm [one]; even when flesh is cut with a weapon, generating ever greater patience — 'I would carry on my head even one who cuts off my hands a hundredfold; and beyond that too, I maintain a mind of loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>).' Patience in contemplating the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmanidhyānakṣānti</s>): not having even a moment's doubt in one's mind when first encountering the exceedingly profound vehicle and the supremely beautiful doctrine of the Sage (<s>Muni</s>). The method of patience in contemplating the <s>Dharma</s> is like that of patience in tolerating abuse. The special distinction here is the non-existence of [external] <s>dharmas</s> [as objects]. As for <s>vīrya</s> (energy), <s>Śāntideva</s> has said:

children.translated_text: [Thus patient, one should cultivate energy (<s>vīrya</s>),] for awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) is established in energy;

children.text: na hi vīryaṃ vinā puṇyaṃ yathā vāyuṃ vinā gatiḥ //
children.translated_text: for without energy there is no merit (<s>puṇya</s>), just as without wind there is no movement.

body.text: kiṃ vīryaṃ kuśalotsāhaḥ / iti /
body.translated_text: What is energy (<s>vīrya</s>)? Zeal for what is wholesome (<s>kuśalotsāha</s>). Thus:

body.text: vīryakaraṇārthadarśī kenacit priyeṇa viyuktaḥ vipriyeṇa ca saṅgataḥ vyādhijarāmaraṇaśokādiduḥkha durgatau patitaḥ [api] sadā kuśalakṣaṇakuśaladṛṣṭiḥ aṣṭasvakṣanasthāneṣu mokṣakāle ca bodhicaryāṃ saṃpaśyan kausīdyaṃ vihāya dṛḍhīkṛtya vimatihīnaḥ duḥkhaprahāṇāya vīryamārabheta //
body.translated_text: One who sees the purpose of practicing energy — even when separated from something dear, joined with what is unpleasant, fallen into the miseries of disease, old age, death, grief, and lower realms of existence — always maintaining a wholesome disposition and a vision of what is wholesome, seeing the <s>Bodhisattva</s>-conduct in the eight unfavorable conditions (<s>akṣaṇa</s>) and at the time of liberation, abandoning laziness, becoming firm, free from doubt — one should undertake energy for the elimination of suffering.

body.text: dhyānam, prajñopāyāvubhau [ekī]kṛtya cittaikāgrīkaraṇaṃ dhyānam // prajñā yathā pūrvoktā // dānapāramitādikaṃ dātṛpratigrahītṛyatkiñcidanālambaṃ śūnyatayā prekṣeta / dānapāramitādi prajñāpāramitayā vyāptam / yathā sūryo dvīpān parivartyaṃ nivartate tathā //
body.translated_text: <s>Dhyāna</s> (meditation): having united both wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) and method (<s>upāya</s>), the one-pointed concentration of the mind is <s>dhyāna</s>. <s>Prajñā</s> (wisdom) is as previously stated. One should regard the <s>dānapāramitā</s> (perfection of giving) and the rest — the giver, recipient, and whatever [is given] — as without support (<s>anālamba</s>), through emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>). The perfection of giving and the rest are pervaded by the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>). Just as the sun revolves around the continents and returns, so too [does wisdom pervade all perfections].

body.text: pāramitāsaṃgrahaḥ / svārthatyāgo dānam / parānugrahaḥ śīlam / gativarjanaṃ kṣamā / kuśalotsāho vīryam / malānupalepo dhyānam / paramārthasatyadeśanāṃ prajñā / sattveṣu karuṇāvyāptīkaraṇaṃ prajñārasaḥ / buddhasādhakaḥ pitṛmātṛduhitṛbandhu parivārapatnyādirājyabhūmyaiśvaryasaukhyādi [ut] śiṣṭānnavat vihāya mokṣārthaṃ vanaṃ gacchet / dānādikantu na duḥkham, buddhalābhasukhaviṣamañca //
body.translated_text: Summary of the <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections): The abandonment of one's own [possessions] is giving (<s>dāna</s>). Benefiting others is moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>). Avoiding [lower] rebirths is patience (<s>kṣamā</s>). Zeal for what is wholesome is energy (<s>vīrya</s>). Non-attachment to defilements is meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>). Teaching the ultimate truth (<s>paramārthasatya</s>) is wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>). Pervading beings with compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>) is the essence of wisdom (<s>prajñārasa</s>). One who accomplishes <s>Buddha</s>-hood — abandoning father, mother, daughter, relatives, retinue, wife, kingship, land, sovereignty, happiness, and the like, as if they were leftover food — should go to the forest for the sake of liberation. But giving and the rest are not [a cause of] suffering; they are incomparable with the happiness of attaining <s>Buddha</s>-hood.

body.text: upāyadeśanāparivartaścaturthaḥ
body.translated_text: The Fourth Chapter: The Teaching of Method (<s>Upāya</s>).

body.text: upāyaprajñayostiṣṭham / iti /
body.translated_text: [One should] abide in [the union of] method (<s>upāya</s>) and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>). Thus:

body.text: prajñā yathā pūrvoktā / katham, pratītyasamutpādena vastuprajñaptilakṣaṇatā / upāyaḥ pūrvoktavaddānādikriyā / tāvubhāvekīkṛtya deśako gururnāsti cet, svapne 'pi [na] utpadyate / evaṃ sati upāyaprajñe dve, tadbhedādvaye jāte punardānādibhede bahavo dāṣāḥ syuriti cet / nāmamātramidaṃ sarvam / upāyaprajñānidarśanaṃ saṃvṛtimātramāśritya siddhyati / [prajñā]pāramitāyāmapyuktam / danapāramitā nāmamātram / prajñāpāramitā nāmamātram / traidhātukamapi nāmamātram // iti /
body.translated_text: Wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) is as previously stated. How? Through dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>), [things have] the character of being mere designations of entities (<s>vastuprajñaptilakṣaṇatā</s>). Method (<s>upāya</s>) is the practice of giving and the rest as previously described. Having united those two — if there is no teacher (<s>guru</s>) who teaches [them as united], then [such understanding] does not arise even in a dream. This being so, method and wisdom are two; but if from their differentiation duality arises, and then from the differentiation of giving etc. there would be many [further divisions] — [in reply:] all this is merely nominal (<s>nāmamātra</s>). The illustration of method and wisdom is established only in dependence on the conventional [level] (<s>saṃvṛtimātra</s>). As is also said in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>: 'The perfection of giving is merely nominal. The perfection of wisdom is merely nominal. The triple world too is merely nominal.' Thus.

body.text:
tadubhayaṃ nirākartumāha /
yato 'bhūdyacca nāma tat / ityādi /
pūrvaṃ parīkṣitavat dharmo nāmamātramucyate / na paramārthato bhāvo 'sti /
dharmatā na sa dharmo 'stīti / iti /
nāmamātratayā siddhaḥ, vastuśūnyatā / pratītyasamutpannaḥ saṃvṛtimātram /
abhūtaṃ nāma śūnyatā / ityādi /
saṃvṛtau nāma nimittamātram / śabdavida āhuḥ / śabdātsarvamutpannamiti / sa svayameva saṃvṛtau nāmamātraṃ siddhaḥ /
body.translated_text: To refute both of those, he says: 'From which it came into being, and that which is called [so],' and so on. As previously examined, a <s>dharma</s> (phenomenon) is said to be mere name. There is no existence in the ultimate sense (<s>paramārtha</s>). The nature of reality (<s>dharmatā</s>) — 'that <s>dharma</s> does not exist.' Thus, [it is] established as mere name — emptiness of substance (<s>vastuśūnyatā</s>). [It is] dependently arisen (<s>pratītyasamutpanna</s>) — mere convention (<s>saṃvṛtimātra</s>). 'What is called the unreal is <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness),' and so on. In convention, a name is a mere designation. The knowers of language say: 'Everything has arisen from words.' That itself is established in convention as mere name.

body.text:
vikalpo yastathoditaḥ / ityādi /
nāmamātram śūnyatā, parīkṣā pūrvavatsugamā /
rūpaṃ taccakṣuṣekṣitam / ityādi /
cakṣū rūpaṃ paśyatītyādi vyākaraṇaṃ bhagavatā saṃvṛtāvuktam /
body.translated_text: 'The conceptualization that is thus stated,' and so on. Mere name is <s>śūnyatā</s>; the analysis is easy as before. 'That form which the eye perceives,' and so on. 'The eye sees form' and such descriptions were stated by the <s>Bhagavān</s> in the conventional [truth].

body.text:
mithyābhimānalokataḥ / ityādi /
abhimānena sattvaṃ deśakālamātrāṃ vāśritya bhagavatā varākisadṛśamuktam / paramārthastvavacanaḥ / paramārthaniścayopāyo mṛṣoktaḥ / duḥkhasatyaṃ duḥkhasamudayasatyaṃ nirodhasatyaṃ mārgasatyamityādyāryasatyāni catvāri saṃvṛtau deśitāni /
body.translated_text: 'From the world of false pride (<s>mithyābhimāna</s>),' and so on. Relying on [mere] sentient existence, place, and time through [false] pride, the <s>Bhagavān</s> spoke, like [speaking to] a wretched person. But the ultimate (<s>paramārtha</s>) is beyond words. The method for ascertaining the ultimate is spoken as false [i.e., provisional]. The <s>Four Noble Truths</s> (<s>āryasatya</s>) — the truth of suffering (<s>duḥkhasatya</s>), the truth of the origin of suffering (<s>duḥkhasamudayasatya</s>), the truth of cessation (<s>nirodhasatya</s>), and the truth of the path (<s>mārgasatya</s>) — were taught in the conventional [truth].

body.text:
darśanaṃ yatpratītyajam / ityādi /
nāyako bhagavato vacanam / rūpaśabdādisamāgamakāmānāṃ sattvānāṃ prakāśayati / yena yān vividhairūpāyaiḥ sattvān vineyān vinayati, tān mocayitvā nayati; tena bhagavān [nāyakaḥ] /
body.translated_text: 'The seeing that is born from conditions,' and so on. The leader (<s>nāyaka</s>) — the word of the <s>Bhagavān</s> — illuminates for beings who desire the conjunction with form, sound, and such. By which, through various skillful means (<s>upāya</s>), he disciplines the beings to be trained, and having liberated them, leads them — therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> is [called] 'the leader.'

body.text:
upacārāvaniṃ satīm / ityādi /
saṃvṛtimāśritya prathabhūmyādyucyate / paramārthabhūmistu sūkṣmabuddhyaparyantā / kalpanāvikalaśūnyatāvediprajñā yasyāsti sa buddhimān / sa ca bhagavān /
body.translated_text: 'The conventional ground being true,' and so on. Relying on convention, the first <s>bhūmi</s> (ground) and so forth are taught. But the ultimate ground is beyond the reach of subtle intelligence. One who possesses the wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) that comprehends emptiness free from conceptual elaboration is wise — and that is the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text:
na cakṣū rūpamīkṣate / ityādi /
taimirika iva cakṣuḥ svayaṃ cakṣū rūpañca na paśyati / sa cittadharmaśca,- cittena citte dṛṣṭamātre cittaṃ na dṛśyate / tena na bhavet / samādhirājasūtre 'pyuktam /
body.translated_text: 'The eye does not perceive form,' and so on. Like one with an eye-disease, the eye itself does not see [itself as] the eye or form. And that is a property of mind (<s>cittadharma</s>) — when mind is seen by mind at the mere moment of seeing, the mind is not [truly] seen. Therefore it would not exist [as seen]. As is also stated in the <s>Samādhirājasūtra</s>:

body.text:
cakṣuḥśrotraghrāṇajivhākāyamanorūpaśabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyadharmā na santi / iti /
tannigamayannāha /
body.translated_text: 'Eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, mind, form, sound, smell, taste, touch, and <s>dharmas</s> do not exist.' Concluding that, he says:

body.text:
sarvaṃ dṛśyaṃ yat / ityādi /
pūrvoktamupāyaprajñobhayaikīkaraṇajñānādikamanṛtamucyate /
body.translated_text: 'All that is visible,' and so on. The aforementioned knowledge unifying both method and wisdom (<s>upāyaprajñā</s>) and the like is said to be unreal.

body.text:
lokaśca vijahāti yat / iti /
tadaviparītaṃ tattvam / lokaḥ prākṛtaḥ yadajānānaḥ yat- cintāpadmabhūtaṃ manasā acintyamindriyāviṣayabhūtamajñānapaṭalāndhakārapratiruddhamadṛṣṭaṃ- tyajati / [sa] paramārthaḥ atitīkṣnendriyaryajñāndṛṣṭigocaraḥ / āryaghanavyūhasūtre /
body.translated_text: 'And that which the world abandons.' That which is not false is reality (<s>tattva</s>). The ordinary world, not knowing that — the lotus of thought that is inconceivable by the mind, beyond the domain of the senses, blocked by the darkness of the veil of ignorance, unseen — abandons it. That is the ultimate (<s>paramārtha</s>), within the range of vision of the <s>Āryas</s> (noble ones) of supremely keen faculties. In the <s>Āryaghanavyūhasūtra</s>:

children.translated_text: Reality is exceedingly wondrous, profound, and infinite;
it is indeed rare — therefore, [it is beyond] the intellect of worldly beings.

body.text:
jñānaṃ tadgocaraṃ nāsti /
saṃvṛtiparamārthasatya [deśanā] parivartaḥ pañcamaḥ
body.translated_text: There is no knowledge that has it as its object. The fifth chapter: the teaching of conventional and ultimate truth (<s>saṃvṛtiparamārthasatya</s>).

body.text: ṣaṭsu jagadgatiṣu bhavasaṅkrāntyupāyo buddhalābhakaropāyaḥ samāptaḥ //
body.translated_text: The method of transition through existence (<s>bhavasaṅkrānti</s>) in the six destinies of beings (<s>jagadgati</s>), the method for attaining Buddhahood, is complete.

body.text: paṇḍitamaitreyanāthakṛtaḥ //
body.translated_text: Composed by the <s>paṇḍita</s> <s>Maitreyanātha</s>.
